definition: Computer-aided detection (CADe), also called computer-aided diagnosis (CADx), are systems that assist doctors in the interpretation of medical images.
details: Imaging techniques in X-ray, MRI, endoscopy, and ultrasound diagnostics yield a great deal of information that the radiologist or other medical professional has to analyze and evaluate comprehensively in a short time. CAD systems process digital images or videos for typical appearances and to highlight conspicuous sections, such as possible diseases, in order to offer input to support a decision taken by the professional. CAD also has potential future applications in digital pathology with the advent of whole-slide imaging and machine learning algorithms. So far its application has been limited to quantifying immunostaining but is also being investigated for the standard H&E stain. CAD is an interdisciplinary technology combining elements of artificial intelligence and computer vision with radiological and pathology image processing. A typical application is the detection of a tumor. For instance, some hospitals use CAD to support preventive medical check-ups in mammography (diagnosis of breast cancer), the detection of polyps in colonoscopy, and lung cancer. explainer.lead: Computer-aided diagnosis uses software to help medical professionals interpret images and videos by pointing out unusual or noteworthy areas. It matters because techniques such as X-ray, MRI, endoscopy, and ultrasound can produce large amounts of information that must be assessed quickly.

tiers.eli5: Imagine looking for a tiny odd shape in a huge picture while a helper circles places worth checking. Computer-aided diagnosis does something similar with medical pictures or videos. A doctor still examines the evidence and makes the decision.
tiers.practitioner: CAD is applied to digital medical images or videos, including X-ray, MRI, endoscopy, and ultrasound, with suspicious regions returned as decision support for a clinician. Typical settings include mammography, colonoscopy, and lung-cancer detection. A highlighted region is not a confirmed disease, and digital-pathology deployments should not assume mature H&E analysis when current use has largely been limited to quantifying immunostaining.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a digital medical image or video I, a CAD system produces decision-support output O, commonly a set of conspicuous structures or sections highlighted for professional review; CADe is usually confined to this marking function. The approach combines artificial intelligence and computer vision with radiological and pathological image processing. In digital pathology, whole-slide imaging and machine learning offer future possibilities, but standard H&E-stain applications remain under investigation.

explainer.example: During a colonoscopy, a CAD system processes the video and highlights a region that may contain a polyp. The medical professional then examines that highlighted area and uses it as input to the clinical decision.

explainer.intuition: CAD acts as a second set of eyes: it searches complex medical imagery for appearances worth attention, then presents those findings to the professional responsible for the decision.
howItWorks: Acquire a digital medical image or video, such as an X-ray, MRI, endoscopy recording, or ultrasound.
Process the imagery for typical appearances and conspicuous structures or sections.
Highlight areas that may indicate disease or otherwise deserve closer review.
Give the marked output to a radiologist or other medical professional as decision-support input.
explainer.whyItMatters: It can help professionals manage information-rich imaging studies by directing attention to conspicuous areas within a short evaluation window. Its role is supportive, combining computational image analysis with professional interpretation.
misconceptions: CAD replaces the doctor: it provides input for a decision made by a medical professional.
Every CADe highlight is a diagnosis: detection systems usually only mark conspicuous structures or sections.
CAD already handles all pathology slides: standard H&E-stain applications are still being investigated.
